in_sanskrit.name: नारायणन्
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Narayanan is a compound name, made up of the words 'nara' meaning 'man' and 'ayana' meaning 'resting place'. In this compound, 'nara' is replaced by the name of the goddess Narayani. So, Narayanan means 'Son of the goddess Narayani'.

data.cultural_impact: Narayanan is a revered name in Hindu culture, signifying protection, love, and devotion towards the supreme god Vishnu, who is also known as Narayana. This name is an embodiment of the divine presence and reflects the deep faith and connection of the people towards their deity. It is often used as a title of respect towards elder members of society and is also commonly used in religious and spiritual contexts.
data.spiritual_significance: Narayanan is a name of deep spiritual significance, representing the ultimate refuge, solace, and protector for all living beings. The name evokes a sense of peace, love, and divine connection. It is believed that invoking the name Narayana or Narayanan can bring about a sense of calm, serenity, and spiritual growth. In Hinduism, the god Narayana is known as the preserver, sustainer, and the ultimate consoler of all beings. The name Narayanan serves as a constant reminder of the divine presence within us and around us, providing strength, hope, and inspiration in times of need.

historical_references.reference: The name Narayanan is derived from the Sanskrit term Narayana, which means 'resting place of the divine'. This term is used to describe Vishnu, one of the principal deities in Hinduism. Narayana is described as the supreme God, who preserves and sustains the universe.

Another reference to the name Narayanan can be found in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. In the Mahabharata, a character named Vidura, who was a wise and just advisor to the Kuru kingdom, is referred to as Narayanan. This usage of the name signifies a divine and wise leader or guide.
